hypothesis: Under a hot-prefix workload, strict prefix-affinity routing will increase cache hit rate but fail a 250 ms p99 latency SLO more often than least-loaded routing, while bounded affinity will retain most of the hit-rate gain without concentrating the hot prefix on one worker.
claimBoundary: The evidence supports a routing trade-off in the declared eight-worker discrete-event simulation with worker-local LRU prefix caches. It cannot establish production GPU throughput, continuous-batching behavior, memory consumption, or the performance of any named inference server.

controls: Uniform-prefix 80 requests per second negative control
Cache-disabled 120 requests per second negative control
Bounded-affinity ablation with a 25 ms queue-slack threshold
